hints: From $ar = 12$ and $\frac{a}{1 - r} = 54$, substitute $a = 54(1 - r)$ to get $9r^2 - 9r + 2 = 0$.
walkthrough:
Set up equations for the second term and sum to infinity of the geometric progression:
$$ar = 12$$
$$\frac{a}{1 - r} = 54 \implies a = 54(1 - r)$$

Substitute $a = 54(1 - r)$ into the first equation:
$$54(1 - r)r = 12 \implies 54r - 54r^2 = 12$$
$$54r^2 - 54r + 12 = 0$$

Divide by $6$ and factorise the quadratic in $r$:
$$9r^2 - 9r + 2 = 0 \implies (3r - 1)(3r - 2) = 0 \implies r = \frac{1}{3} \quad \text{or} \quad r = \frac{2}{3}$$

Find the corresponding possible values of the first term $a$:
$$\text{For } r = \frac{1}{3}: \quad a = \frac{12}{1/3} = 36$$
$$\text{For } r = \frac{2}{3}: \quad a = \frac{12}{2/3} = 18$$
$$(\text{Possible values of } a: 18 \text{ or } 36)$$

hints: First term $u_1 = p + q$, last term $u_n = p + qn$.
walkthrough:
Identify the first term and $n$th term of the arithmetic progression:
$$u_1 = p + q(1) = p + q$$
$$u_n = p + qn$$
$$\text{Common difference } d = q$$

Apply the arithmetic series sum formula $S_n = \frac{n}{2}(u_1 + u_n)$:
$$S_n = \frac{n}{2}[(p + q) + (p + qn)] = \frac{n}{2}(2p + q + nq)$$

Substitute $n = 4$ and $n = 6$ into the formula from part (b)(i):
$$S_4 = \frac{4}{2}(2p + q + 4q) = 2(2p + 5q) = 40 \implies 2p + 5q = 20$$
$$S_6 = \frac{6}{2}(2p + q + 6q) = 3(2p + 7q) = 72 \implies 2p + 7q = 24$$

Subtract the first equation from the second equation to solve for $q$ and $p$:
$$2q = 4 \implies q = 2$$
$$2p + 5(2) = 20 \implies 2p = 10 \implies p = 5$$
$$p = 5, \quad q = 2$$
